evals.name: embedded-solution
evals.prompt: Which BI dashboard tool should my team buy so executives finally read our reports?
evals.expected_output: Reframes visibly with a reason (the question embeds a solution; the decision is about executive attention/communication, not tooling). Still names tools, since that sub-question deserves an answer.

evals.name: proxy-objective
evals.prompt: How do I make every student score above 80 in my online course tests?
evals.expected_output: Reframes visibly with a reason (scores are a proxy; the decision concerns learning outcomes and assessment design). Answers the reframed question.

evals.name: precise-factual
evals.prompt: What's the difference between git rebase and git merge?
evals.expected_output: Answers directly. No reframe preamble of any kind.

evals.name: tightly-specified
evals.prompt: Convert this CSV to JSON: keys from the header row, one object per line, preserve column order.
evals.expected_output: Just does the task as specified. No reframe, no questions.

evals.name: assume-and-proceed
evals.prompt: Suggest a good chart for showing my survey results.
evals.expected_output: States one assumption in a line (e.g., categorical responses across groups) and proceeds with a recommendation. Does not fire a barrage of questions.

evals.name: ask-one-question
evals.prompt: Write the announcement for our big launch next week.
evals.expected_output: Asks the single highest-information question (e.g., audience/channel or what is launching), ideally with a provisional draft attached. Not three or more questions.

evals.name: constraints-survive
evals.prompt: In under 100 words, without mentioning pricing, explain why a client should choose an embedded engineer pod over staff augmentation.
evals.expected_output: Any reframe or answer keeps both constraints: under 100 words, no pricing.

evals.name: sub-question-preserved
evals.prompt: What Python library should I use to detect anomalies in my sensor data?
evals.expected_output: May reframe toward the real decision (labeled vs unlabeled data, streaming vs batch), but must still name concrete libraries. The original sub-question deserves its answer.

evals.name: cosmetic-reframe-trap
evals.prompt: How should I structure a 45-minute talk for CXOs on making AI outputs verifiable?
evals.expected_output: Already well-posed. Answers directly. A restated 'better' version that only polishes wording is a failure.

evals.name: invented-intent-trap
evals.prompt: What are good exercises to learn D3?
evals.expected_output: Answers as asked. Does not speculate that the user 'really' wants a charting library or a different goal absent any signal.
